challenger.name: Book-Rate Turnaround and Booked-Appointment Desk for PE-Backed Home-Services Platforms
challenger.thesis: PE platforms that bought roughly 800 HVAC/plumbing/electrical shops run CSR book rates of 50-75% with only 35% of agents asking for the booking, so a 90-day book-rate turnaround ($25K-60K per platform) followed by a managed overflow/after-hours/outbound rehash desk priced per booked job ($15-40 each) converts directly into EBITDA the sponsor is hunting for.
challenger.why_now: The 'roll-up of the roll-ups' is expected within 18 months, forcing platforms to show operating gains before sale; the home-services gold rush is over and 'who can actually run a business' is the 2026 story; ServiceTitan Contact Center Pro case studies show 13% booking lifts but require operators to realize them.

dossier.key_numbers: PE platforms bought ~800 shops; book rates 50-75% (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Nexstar/CertainPath and ServiceTitan analytics sell the same fix; needs a PE-platform network. Survives.

incumbent.name: Show-rate guarantee desk: performance-based no-show reduction and dormant-patient reactivation for high-ticket consult businesses
incumbent.thesis: Med spas, dental-implant and ortho centers, LASIK, solar/roofing/HVAC-replacement sales, and membership-tour operators lose 25-40% of booked consults to no-shows; an outsourced confirmation-and-rescue desk (AI voice + SMS first-pass confirmations, deposit capture, human rescue calls, same-day waitlist backfill, rebook-on-cancel) sold at $40-150 per kept appointment or a $3-8K/mo retainer can clear $1-3M/yr with 15-25 seats of cheap Texarkana labor, because one kept implant or solar consult is worth $3-8K to the client and they already measure show rate as a KPI.
incumbent.why_now: AI voice agents now do first-pass confirmations for roughly $0.10/min, consumer no-show rates never recovered after 2020, and every lead-gen client is paying more per booked appointment as ad costs rise, so a guaranteed-show layer is the cheapest lift available. Joshua runs this exact function today (dialers, reps, show rates) and can sell it as a productized service on day one.

dossier.key_numbers: no-shows 20-40% of high-ticket consults; performance fee per recovered show (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Attribution disputes on performance pricing; AI confirmation bots erode the labor moat; clients churn once rates improve. Fit is perfect, moat is thin. Survives.

pairing_reason: same kind of business: outsourced appointment desk; only one should hold a slot

challenger.name: Dialer Migration and Telecom Cost-Audit Practice (CCaaS implementation plus contingency carrier-bill recovery)
challenger.thesis: Every call center replatforms its dialer/CCaaS every 3-5 years and overpays carriers 10-25% on SIP trunks, DIDs and unused seats, so charge $15K-60K per migration (Convoso, Five9, Readymode, Genesys, HubSpot/GHL integrations), take 30-50% contingency on telecom savings found, and keep each client on a $2K-5K/mo admin retainer.
challenger.why_now: CCaaS vendors are shipping AI features in 2026 that force replatforming, contact centers are consolidating tools to cut costs, and vendor professional-services teams cannot keep up with migrations, so certified implementation partners are being courted with margin.

dossier.key_numbers: $15-60K per migration plus 10-25% carrier-bill recovery (generator source; his own Convoso dialer-impact work)
dossier.skeptic: Vendor partner networks and SIs compete; a few migrations a year; employer conflict. Survives.

incumbent.name: Outbound contact-rate and TCPA / mini-TCPA compliance managed service for lead-gen call centers (DID reputation, branded calling, litigator scrub, Texas SB 140 desk)
incumbent.thesis: Outbound call centers lose half their answers to 'Spam Likely' labels and cannot run number-reputation operations themselves, so a boutique that owns DID inventory strategy, carrier registrations, Rich Call Data / branded caller ID setup, remediation tickets, rotation and weekly reputation monitoring bills $3K-10K/mo per client plus per-DID fees and proves ROI with answer-rate lift.
incumbent.why_now: January 2026 alone saw 3.9B robocalls, 53% of enterprise leaders report improper spam labels cutting contact rates, and branded calls answer at 62% vs 20% unbranded; carriers now sell RCD and branded display, but SMB call centers have nobody to operate it.

dossier.key_numbers: contact centers lose half their answers to spam labels; DID reputation ops sold as a managed service (generator source; his own DID dashboard is the product)
dossier.skeptic: Numeracle and Caller ID Reputation sell tooling, not ops, so the boutique gap is real; clients must be found outside his employer; attribution of contact-rate lift. Survives; strongest fit in the pool.

pairing_reason: both sell services to call centers

challenger.name: Spreadsheet-to-App Studio: fixed-price internal tool replacement for mid-size companies
challenger.thesis: Mid-size companies run on Excel plus email plus a $40K/year per-seat SaaS they hate; a solo builder using agentic coding can replace one workflow with a custom web app in two weeks for a $15K-$40K fixed fee plus $1-3K/month hosting and support, and 12-18 projects a year is a $400K+ business with no employees.
challenger.why_now: Agentic coding tools in 2026 let one person ship in days what took a five-person shop a quarter; the 'build not buy' shift is being modeled publicly by companies cutting SaaS seats; and a portfolio of already-shipped apps and ops dashboards is the credibility that closes these deals without a sales team.

dossier.key_numbers: $15-40K fixed-price internal-tool projects (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Every agency now claims this; buyers can vibe-code too; needs a local business network to sell. Survives.

incumbent.name: Forward-deployed AI engineer / AI implementation contractor (voice and contact-center AI vendors)
incumbent.thesis: FDE job listings spiked ~800% with total comp of $200K-$630K+ (https://www.paraform.com/insights/forward-deployed-ai-engineer), a competent mid-level FDE earns $180-260K (https://www.recruitingfromscratch.com/blog/forward-deployed-engineer-salary-in-2026-full-guide) and Palantir's FDSE median is $215K (https://getperspective.ai/blog/2026-forward-deployed-engineering-compensation-report-1200-fdes); someone who ships production apps with AI coding tools AND has lived inside a call center is exactly the deploy-into-the-customer profile, and the same skills sell as 12-24 month implementation contracts at $60-86/hr (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Ai-Implementation-Specialist).
incumbent.why_now: Voice AI specialists earn $39-60/hr median with 25-40% premiums for LLM fine-tuning and AI engineer base pay averages $206K in 2026 (https://callsphere.ai/blog/vw9c-ai-voice-engineer-hiring-market-2026-salaries-comp); BCG X now hires Forward Deployed AI Engineers straight from campus at $110-190K, showing the role has gone mainstream beyond Palantir (https://managementconsulted.com/bcg-forward-deployed-ai-engineer/); domain expertise in contact centers is the scarce half of the FDE skill pair.

dossier.key_numbers: FDE median base $190-207K, mid-level TC $180-260K, postings up ~800% (https://www.levels.fyi/t/software-engineer/title/forward-deployed-engineer; recruitingfromscratch.com)
dossier.skeptic: Technical interviews screen for real engineering depth, not AI-assisted shipping; equity-heavy at the top. The 1099 implementation-contractor path ($100-200/hr) is the reachable version. Survives.

pairing_reason: both are software/AI implementation for businesses

challenger.name: Estate cleanout, hoarder and unattended-death cleanup company
challenger.thesis: Heirs, executors, landlords and realtors pay $2K-$15K per job to make a house empty and sellable fast, hoarder and biohazard jobs run $5K-$30K with insurance often covering them, and the labor is a trailer, a dumpster account, PPE and two crew members.
challenger.why_now: The largest generation in US history is hitting its mortality peak over the next decade with houses full of 50 years of stuff, kids live in other states and cannot take a week off to sort it, and the incumbents are junk haulers who will not touch the sensitive, embarrassing, or biological jobs that carry the highest margins.

dossier.key_numbers: $2-15K per cleanout, $5-30K biohazard, insurance often pays (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Unglamorous but proven; competition from Aftermath/Bio-One franchises; needs biohazard training. Survives.

incumbent.name: Roll-off dumpster rental fleet with online self-booking
incumbent.thesis: One used hook-lift truck (~$80-100K) and fifteen steel cans (~$5-6K each) throw off $450-650 per haul plus tonnage overage, so a single driver-owner can gross $250-400K a year at 50%+ margins in a secondary market the national haulers ignore for small jobs.
incumbent.why_now: The owner-operators who built these routes in the 1990s are aging out and selling, ArkLaTex hail/tornado/flood rebuild cycles keep demand spiky, steel tariffs have pushed new-can prices up (protecting incumbents who already own iron), and WM/Republic still won't do a 10-yard driveway can on 24 hours notice. Real capital need: ~$120-150K, financeable with $25-35K down.

dossier.key_numbers: one-truck owner earnings $120-250K, $350-450K revenue with a driver, ~$90K to start, 18-24 month payback (https://www.curbwaste.com/dumpster-rental-business-profitability; quipli.com)
dossier.skeptic: Tipping fees, truck downtime and WM/Republic pricing; still one of the best-documented cash businesses at this capital level. Survives.

pairing_reason: both are unglamorous cash businesses with a truck

challenger.name: Cost-Segregation Study Firm riding permanent 100% bonus depreciation
challenger.thesis: The One Big Beautiful Bill (P.L. 119-21) made 100% bonus depreciation permanent for property placed in service after Jan 19, 2025 and created 100% expensing for Qualified Production Property, both of which require a cost-segregation study as the substantiating document (https://www.cbh.com/insights/articles/trumps-tax-bill-bonus-depreciation-cost-segregation/); studies bill $5K-$15K for commercial buildings, about $10K per $1M property, and owners typically get a 4x-10x first-year return on the fee (https://www.recostseg.com/post/cost-seg-pricing-5k-vs-15k; https://corporatetaxadvisors.com/cost-of-cost-segregation-study-complete-pricing-guide-for-2026/). A firm with one engineer plus a CPA-referral sales channel doing 150 studies/yr is ~$1.5M in revenue (estimate).
challenger.why_now: Permanence removed the phase-down that would have hit zero by 2027 (Cherry Bekaert link above), so every 2025-2026 acquisition and every new manufacturing facility (QPP construction must begin before Jan 1, 2029) needs a study now. FIT: medium-high - outbound prospecting to CPAs and investors plus a software front end for intake; engineering can be subcontracted.

dossier.key_numbers: $5-13K per residential/small-multifamily study, $12-60K commercial; 100% bonus depreciation now permanent under OBBBA (https://www.baselane.com/resources/cost-segregation-bonus-depreciation)
dossier.skeptic: Needs engineering-based credibility (or a partner); national firms and $99 AI estimates compress the small end; sold through CPAs. Survives; strong ceiling.

incumbent.name: Diesel generator load-bank testing and fuel polishing for data centers, hospitals and telecom sites
incumbent.thesis: NFPA 110 and Joint Commission rules require annual load-bank tests and clean fuel on every backup generator, each visit bills $1,500-6,000, and there are thousands of new generators being installed across Texas and the South with almost no independent local testers.
incumbent.why_now: ERCOT's large-load queue has exploded past 100 GW of data-center and industrial requests, every one of those sites is installing rows of diesel gensets that must be tested and have fuel polished on a schedule, and the OEM service networks are backlogged months. Capital: $40-70K for a trailer-mounted resistive load bank and a fuel-polishing rig.

dossier.key_numbers: NFPA 110 annual load-bank tests; $1,500-6,000 per visit (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Needs generator/electrical competence and facility-manager relationships; safety liability. Mandated recurring demand is real and growing with data centers. Survives.

pairing_reason: both trend-driven specialty B2B service businesses

challenger.name: Medicare Advantage telesales agency building a renewal book (CMS fixed commissions)
challenger.thesis: CMS sets the maximum broker payment at $694 per new Medicare Advantage enrollment plus $347/yr renewal for 2026, rising to $725/$363 in 2027, with PDP at $114/$57 (https://ritterim.com/blog/2027-maximum-broker-commissions-for-medicare-advantage-and-medicare-part-d/) - paid by carriers, never by the senior - so a compliant licensed agency running 10 agents at 40 applications/month builds a renewal annuity. Estimate: 4,800 enrollments/yr x $694 = ~$3.3M first-year commissions plus ~$1.67M/yr in renewals per retained cohort (basis: CMS 2026 rates above; agent productivity assumed).
challenger.why_now: Peak 65: a record 4.18M Americans turned 65 in 2025 (11,400/day) (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/the-us-has-reached-the-peak-of-peak-65-its-time-to-apply-retirement-readiness-lessons-from-the-boomer-experience-302360086.html) and ~4.1M more turn 65 in 2026 with the surge running through 2027 (https://natlawreview.com/press-releases/4-million-americans-turn-65-2026-ltc-news-expands-free-tools-aging-and-long); CMS raised max compensation for 2026 and again for 2027 (Ritter). FIT: very high - licensed telesales with dialers, scripts, and QA is Joshua's core competency; TCPA/CMS marketing rules are the moat.

dossier.key_numbers: CMS 2026 max $694 initial / $347 renewal per MA member; 500-member book = ~$173K/yr renewals; 10 apps/month compounds to $150K+ by year 4 (https://ritterim.com/blog/2027-maximum-broker-commissions-for-medicare-advantage-and-medicare-part-d/; medicareagentshub.com)
dossier.skeptic: Lead costs $30-60, carriers cutting commissions on some plans, TPMO recording rules, rapid-disenrollment chargebacks; year-2 net is modest but the book compounds and is sellable. Survives; best fit-plus-durability pairing in the pool.

incumbent.name: Recurring-route pest control company built to 80%+ contract revenue (PE-exit spec)
incumbent.thesis: Launch for $15-65K all-in, break even in 6-14 months, and take home $80-140K by year two as a solo operator in a 200K+ metro (https://oncallclerk.com/blog/how-to-start-a-pest-control-business); 150 quarterly accounts at $80-120/visit is $480-720 per customer per year at 20-40% net margins (same source); then stack routes to $1M+ EBITDA, where 85%-recurring, sub-1.5%-monthly-churn books command 6.5-8x EBITDA and the recurring mix alone is worth a $2M valuation swing on a $1M-EBITDA business (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/pest-control-business-valuation/).
incumbent.why_now: $29.7B US market with 34,000+ operators and PE at ~60% of all pest M&A, with Anticimex, Arrow and Massey still aggressively acquisitive (https://www.breakwaterma.com/blog/pest-control-company-valuation-multiples-2026); pest control carries a 3.3x low / 5-6x mid / 8x+ high EBITDA band, top of the home-services stack (https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/home-services-ma-multiples-report-2026/). Fit: route density is a lead-gen and dialer problem — Joshua's day job — and his RV-resort employer is a ready-made commercial anchor account.

dossier.key_numbers: solo take-home $80-140K by year 2, gross $135-300K, 25-50% margin once routed (https://www.fieldroutes.com/blog/how-profitable-is-pest-control-business; oncallclerk.com)
dossier.skeptic: Route density and a TDA applicator license are the gates; metros are crowded but Ark-La-Tex is not. Numbers hold. Survives.

challenger.name: Contingency B2B collections / AR-recovery agency for contractors, trucking and medical practices
challenger.thesis: Construction carries roughly a quarter-trillion dollars in late receivables and the average subcontractor waits 80+ days to get paid; a pre-litigation AR desk that runs AI-written dunning cadences, files preliminary lien and bond-claim notices, and makes human collection calls, taking 15-25% of collected dollars or a $500-2K/mo retainer, does $1-3M/yr on 100 clients because every trade contractor has $50-500K sitting uncollected and no one on staff to chase it.
challenger.why_now: 2025-26 payment delays hit record highs as construction credit tightened, lien-notice and prompt-payment statutes give real leverage, AI personalizes demand sequences at near-zero cost, and Texarkana phone labor plus Joshua's dialer operations make the human layer cheap and scalable.

dossier.key_numbers: 25-35% contingency on $5K-100K commercial invoices; construction AR waits 80+ days (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Texas requires a $10K surety bond; recovery rates 20-30%; slow ramp to a book of clients. Survives.

challenger.name: Rural septic pumping + real-estate septic inspection + aerobic-maintenance contract route
challenger.thesis: A used vacuum truck runs $40-120K (https://www.septictrucks.com/how-much-does-a-septic-truck-cost-in-2026-real-prices-and-buyer-guide/), each residential pump-out bills $300-600, and owner-operators run 50-65% gross / 20-35% net margins (https://www.septictankhub.com/blog/is-septic-business-profitable/) — one truck grosses $75-300K, 2-5 trucks $500K-2M+ (https://servicecore.com/blog/owning-a-septic-pumping-business-salary/). The recurring kicker: Texas requires every aerobic system to carry a $200-500/yr maintenance contract with inspections every 4 months by a TCEQ-licensed provider, backed by fines up to $100/day (https://www.texassepticguide.com/learn/aerobic-septic-maintenance-texas) — a legally mandated subscription book.
challenger.why_now: Texas has ~2.6 million septic systems and demand is growing faster than almost anywhere in the country as housing pushes into rural counties (https://septicandwell.com/articles/septic-system-texas); the TCEQ Installer I license needs only a $460 TEEX course, a $111 fee and an exam with no prior experience, and Installer II (aerobic systems) follows after one year (https://www.servicetitan.com/licensing/septic/texas); the trade is described as low-competition, high-profit (https://www.ownedandoperated.com/post/how-to-start-a-septic-business). Fit: an RV-resort membership company is a built-in commercial septic customer.

dossier.key_numbers: solo owners $50-150K, net margin 20-35%, $400-500 per pump-out, used truck $70-110K (https://www.curbwaste.com/owning-a-septic-pumping-business-salary; servicecore.com)
dossier.skeptic: Dirty, physical, truck-capital business; disposal fees eat margin. Income claim holds at the low-100s. Survives.

Real capital need: ~$120-150K, financeable with $25-35K down.

dossier.skeptic: Tipping fees, truck downtime and WM/Republic pricing; still one of the best-documented cash businesses at this capital level. Survives.

challenger.name: Texas property-tax protest firm (contingency, dialer-driven mass enrollment, own comps engine)
challenger.thesis: Texas local governments levied a record $125.05B in property taxes in 2024 (https://www.texaspolicyresearch.com/texas-property-tax-levies-1998-2025/); protest firms keep 25% (Ownwell) to 35-50% (traditional firms) of first-year savings with zero upfront fee (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/property-tax-protest-companies-cost), 60-80% of protests statewide win (https://propertytaxdesk.com/texas/property-tax-appeal-complete-guide/), and roughly 71% of DFW homeowners never filed in 2025 (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/protest-property-taxes-texas) - so a TDLR-licensed property-tax-consultant shop with an outbound dialer signs the non-filers and collects a slice of every reduction, every year, with no inventory and near-zero cost of goods.
challenger.why_now: Texas levies rose another $2.7B in 2025 (https://texastaxpayers.com/texas-property-taxes-increased-2-7-billion-in-2025-whats-broken-and-how-do-we-actually-fix-it/), so the savings pool grows annually, and the fixed May 15 protest deadline (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/protest-property-taxes-texas) turns it into a predictable yearly outbound campaign. FIT: very high - this is a lead-gen + dialer + show-rate business, the exact machine Joshua runs by day.

dossier.key_numbers: firms charge 25-50% of first-year savings (https://www.ownwell.com/blog/property-tax-protest-companies-cost); Texas levied $125B in 2024 (texaspolicyresearch.com)
dossier.skeptic: TDLR property-tax-consultant registration; Ownwell/O'Connor own the metros; Bowie County values are low so fees per account are small; 2025 homestead exemption raise cut homeowner savings. Survives as a volume business.

challenger.name: Senior Living Placement Agency (facility-paid referral fees, run like a call-center booking desk)
challenger.thesis: Assisted-living communities pay placement agencies 70-80% of a resident's first month's rent, typically $3,000-5,000 per move-in, in a U.S. senior-living market on pace to pass $980B in 2026 with more than 32,000 assisted-living communities competing for move-ins (https://beancount.io/blog/2026/07/19/senior-living-placement-agency-referral-fee-revenue-recognition-guide): a two-person team closing 10 placements a month is a $360K-600K/yr business with almost no fixed cost (my arithmetic on the per-placement range).
challenger.why_now: By 2026 nearly one in five Americans is 65+ with ~61.2M people 65 and older (https://www.premierhcinc.com/blog/home-care-statistics/) and ~11,400 boomers age in daily (https://elitemedfinancials.com/nemt-industry-statistics/); the 80+ cohort that actually moves into assisted living is the fastest-growing slice of the decade, and communities' occupancy pressure keeps referral fees high. Capital: under $25K. Ceiling is limited only by advisor headcount and territory, and it cross-sells directly into home care and CAPS remodeling.

dossier.key_numbers: 70-80% of first month's rent, $3-5K per placement; APFM charges $3.5-12K (https://www.seniorliving.org/placement-agencies/)
dossier.skeptic: FTC ANPRM March 2026 and state disclosure laws; A Place for Mom dominance; lead cost. Survives with regulatory risk.

pairing_reason: both call-center booking desks paid on outcome

challenger.name: Contingency denial-recovery and appeals shop for independent practices
challenger.thesis: Claim denial rates run 12-15% and most denied claims are never re-worked because the practice cannot afford the 45 minutes per appeal; a firm that takes only aged and denied claims, writes payer-specific, clinically cited appeals with AI, and has humans work the phone and prior-auth follow-ups, paid 20-30% of dollars recovered, can pull $2-5M/yr from 30-50 practice clients at 50%+ margin because the AI turns a 45-minute appeal into a 5-minute review.
challenger.why_now: Payers now auto-deny with AI (UnitedHealth, Cigna, Humana litigation), the CMS 2026 prior-authorization interoperability rule and WISeR model add new friction, 2026 Medicare fee cuts squeeze margins, and LLMs finally write medical-necessity appeals that cite policy and clinical guidelines well enough to win.

dossier.key_numbers: denials 12-15% of claims, two-thirds never appealed (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Needs a certified biller/coder on staff; RCM AI vendors (Waystar, Adonis) sell to the same practices. Survives.

incumbent.name: Show-rate guarantee desk: performance-based no-show reduction and dormant-patient reactivation for high-ticket consult businesses
incumbent.thesis: Med spas, dental-implant and ortho centers, LASIK, solar/roofing/HVAC-replacement sales, and membership-tour operators lose 25-40% of booked consults to no-shows; an outsourced confirmation-and-rescue desk (AI voice + SMS first-pass confirmations, deposit capture, human rescue calls, same-day waitlist backfill, rebook-on-cancel) sold at $40-150 per kept appointment or a $3-8K/mo retainer can clear $1-3M/yr with 15-25 seats of cheap Texarkana labor, because one kept implant or solar consult is worth $3-8K to the client and they already measure show rate as a KPI.
incumbent.why_now: AI voice agents now do first-pass confirmations for roughly $0.10/min, consumer no-show rates never recovered after 2020, and every lead-gen client is paying more per booked appointment as ad costs rise, so a guaranteed-show layer is the cheapest lift available. Joshua runs this exact function today (dialers, reps, show rates) and can sell it as a productized service on day one.

dossier.key_numbers: no-shows 20-40% of high-ticket consults; performance fee per recovered show (generator source)
dossier.skeptic: Attribution disputes on performance pricing; AI confirmation bots erode the labor moat; clients churn once rates improve. Fit is perfect, moat is thin. Survives.

pairing_reason: both outsourced desks for medical practices
